newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi tells Italian bureaucrats to economise.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi tells Italian bureaucrats to economise.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has ordered Italian bureaucrats to cut down on telephone calls and newspapers as part of his drive to brake the country's public spending, newspapers reported on Wednesday.

Ciampi, who last week unveiled a 15.5 trillion lire ($9.3 billion) package of additional budget austerity measures for this year, has sent a circular to state administration offices telling them 1998 running costs must not grow more than one percent on 1997, the reports said.

That meant savings on "contributions of a discretionary nature to public bodies and associations", travel expenses and a "drastic reduction" in newspapers, telephones, car maintenance and "every other cost which can be eliminated or cut".

Italy's centre-left government is trying to contain its budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in an effort to squeeze into economic parameters for joining a European single currency in 1999.

The deficit was 6.7 percent of GDP in 1996 but Prime Minister Romano Prodi says his mini-budget unveiled last week, which comes on top of a hefty 62.5 trillion lire full-year 1997 package, will be enough to meet the single currency criteria.
"The ceiling set by Ciampi regards the whole mass of state running costs," La Repubblica daily said.
It said expenditure this year was 450 trillion and the one percent ceiling corresponded to half of the target inflation rate for 1998 of two percent.
Ciampi said spending on goods and services in 1999 must also be kept to one percent while for the year 2000 it must stay below two percent, Il Sole financial daily reported.
Capital spending was limited to 2.5 percent for the next three years.
